transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-09
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Asha (Redwood SE), Priya (VertexHealth Head of ML), Carlos (Eng Manager), Lena (Product), Tom (Security)

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we wanted to use the first ten minutes to make sure we're aligned on success criteria for the POC and then dig into model selection. is that still the right agenda?
00:18 Priya: Yeah that works. I'm mainly curious about quality tradeoffs — like we need high accuracy on clinical terms and also Spanish and Portuguese support for our LATAM users. Latency is important but accuracy wins if it's clinically material.
00:35 Maya: totally. Maybe Jonah you can run through what we've seen for similar customers and the typical tradeoffs?
00:40 Jonah: Sure. So in general for open-model POCs we recommend starting with 2-3 variants: a smaller low-latency model for interactive flows and a medium / larger model for quality checks. For example people try Llama 2/3 13B-ish or Mistral 7B in an optimized quant and then a Falcon-40B type for heavy quality. The main tradeoffs are 1) latency — bigger models -> higher p95 unless you GPU-scale, 2) token cost, 3) multilingual performance which varies a lot.
01:08 Carlos: when you say p95, what's realistic? We're targeting sub 200ms p95 for the UI path — is that feasible?
01:16 Jonah: Sub-200ms p95 is ambitious for any non-sharded 13B on shared infra. On dedicated with batching / KV cache we can get 150-220ms for a 13B with short prompts. For a 40B you'd be in 400-700ms unless you do sequence shorter or distill. There's also smart routing — you can route <200ms traffic to a small model and fall back to larger model for background checks.
01:38 Priya: Our success criteria: 1) Summaries must have >90% clinical term accuracy on our labeled set, 2) Interactive latency <250ms p95 for triage UI, 3) cost target under $0.015 per user session (rough estimate), 4) support for EN/ES/PT — Spanish primary for LATAM pilot.
01:58 Maya: great, we'll capture that. For benchmarking we'll define both quantitative metrics (p95 latency, token cost, F1 on clinical entities) and qualitative scoring with your clinicians.
02:10 Lena: on workload sizing — we expect 40k active users in pilot month but concurrency is spiky; typical bursts up to 150 rps for short requests, average 30 rps. Will that change model choices?
02:24 Jonah: yes, bursty high rps favors smaller models and aggressive batching or dedicated pools. Redwood Dedicated or a reserved pool in private mode helps guarantee throughput. For POC we can simulate your burst profile to estimate cost.
02:36 Tom: security note: we need to confirm data residency and KMS integration. We will need SOC2 plus logs for audits. Can you share your security pack?
02:46 Maya: absolutely, we'll send our security docs. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated, and audit logs are available. We'll include the SOC2 and penetration test summary.
03:00 Jonah: back to models — here's a proposed shortlist for the POC: Llama 3 13B-instruct (if available), Mistral-Instruct 7B, Falcon-40B-Instruct for quality baseline, and MPT-30B-Instruct as a cost/quality mid-point. We also recommend a distilled or quantized 7B as the interactive model.
03:23 Priya: are there known issues with medical terms across these? Any model that stands out for Spanish medical vocab?
03:29 Jonah: Mistral and some fine-tuned Llama variants tend to do well on European Spanish; Falcon often needs few-shot anchor prompts. There's noise in transcription for abbreviations — we may need to add prompt engineering and a small domain fine-tune or adapter.
03:45 Carlos: will we need fine-tuning? That will add time and compliance complexity.
03:50 Jonah: not necessarily; many customers use in-context learning + prompt sets and a small retrieval augmentation to hit high precision for clinical terms. If you want >=95% entity accuracy across edge cases, we might recommend a 10k-100k example domain tune or a supervised adapter. We can scope that as part of the POC.
04:10 Priya: timeline question — how long to run the benchmarks? We need statistically meaningful results across our workflows and languages.
04:18 Asha: Our suggested POC timeline: 1) 1 week kick-off and infra setup, 2) 2 weeks automated benchmarking across prompts and languages, 3) 1 week clinician qualitative review, 4) 1 week iteration (prompt + small retune) = ~5 weeks. If you add a fine-tune step add 2-3 weeks.
04:34 Lena: that aligns. For benchmarks we want both synthetic throughput tests and real prompt latencies.
04:40 Jonah: yes, we'll run both: synthetic load tests to validate throughput and on-calls traces for p95 matching your UI. Also we'll run token-cost simulations. We'll share a spreadsheet with expected cost per 1k sessions for each model + quantization level.
04:56 Priya: what's your recommended quantization for 13B/40B? We care about quality degradation.
05:02 Jonah: For 13B we see 4-bit quant (q4) giving near-native quality for many tasks; q2 is riskier but lower cost. For 40B, q4 is common but you can see more hallucination sometimes. We'll benchmark q4 and int8 when supported.
05:17 Carlos: I want to call out retrieval augmentation — can we pair the models with a vector DB and selective retrieval for clinical knowledge?
05:24 Jonah: absolutely — retrieval plus a short context can dramatically improve clinical recall; Redwood Optimize can suggest cache and batching configs. We'll also test a retrieval-augmented pipeline vs plain generation.
05:36 Tom: on compliance — when you run the benchmark on Redwood Dedicated, does data stay in our VPC?
05:41 Maya: yes for Private and Dedicated options the data plane can be customer-managed; we'll document the exact flow. We'll also provide details on KMS integration for key rotation.
05:50 Priya: ok sounds good. Are there any low-effort experiments we can do in week one to get early signals?
05:56 Jonah: yes run a 1k-prompt smoke with your top 10 prompts across languages against Mistral-7B and Llama-13B-instruct in quantized mode; that will give quick quality and latency signals.
06:08 Maya: fantastic. Quick recap and action items...
06:12 Maya: Redwood to send model shortlist, benchmark plan, security docs, and pilot pricing. VertexHealth to share labeled eval set + prompts and compliance contact. We'll aim to start benchmarks week of 2025-05-19.
06:23 Priya: agreed. One last thing — competitors and comparisons are useful; can you include a short note vs OpenAI API / Anthropic on cost/latency tradeoffs?
06:33 Maya: yes we'll add a short appendix comparing hosted OpenAI/Anthropic pricing and latency characteristics and highlight where an open-model Dedicated route gives cost benefits.
06:40 Carlos: thanks all, excited to get started.
06:43 Maya: thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with materials.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-hears in automated transcript (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache, "Llama three" sometimes transcribed as "llama tree"). Some speaker labels merged due to call system.
